title: Study questions: How broadly should the statutory interest be defined?
shortTitle: Study questions: How broadly should the statutory interest be defined?
summary: Compare NCUA’s market-limitation rationale with the dissent’s concern that incidental benefits would erase the zone-of-interests requirement.
notes:
NCUA identifies an interest in limiting credit-union customer markets. Its dissent identifies the provision’s internal cooperative and financial-stability purposes. Explain why the chosen level of description matters and what evidence in the statutory text and operation supports each account.

Apply both approaches to Air Courier’s postal employees, the hypothetical stenographer harmed by omitted on-the-record hearings, and Twin Rivers’s paper companies. Then explain why Thompson and Patchak satisfied the test under the supplied descriptions. Distinguish injury in fact from membership in the statutory zone at every step. This comparative exercise follows the opposing opinions and examples in the assigned material; it is explanatory synthesis rather than a quoted syllabus problem.
